title: L-functions and physics: notes on Dirichlet L-functions, the zeta function and physical models
description: Short notes, with figures and checking scripts, on where Dirichlet L-functions, the Riemann zeta function and their characters appear in physical settings: the characters of the modular group and the twelve-tone scale; quadratic characters, lattice sums, Talbot diffraction and Schroeder diffusers; light and the hydrogen spectrum; what an L-function is and looks like; the golden ratio; towards a number-theoretic standard model (conjectures with exact evidence); impulses, packets and spectra (primes and zeros as a Fourier pair); the speed of light, the light cone and spheres; the zeros as energy levels (random-matrix statistics, the trace formula, independent spectra). Each statement is graded (proved in Lean, classical, computed, convention, open).
